correctness.rationale: Slice y=±ts gives a rectangle with area 4t(1−s)² and mean x²=t²(1−s)²/3, so the volume mean is t²/5. The eight triangular facets comprise four with area t√(t²+1) and barycentric mean t²/6, four with area t√2 and mean t²/2. Their area-weighted difference from the volume mean is t²(9√2−√(t²+1))/[30(√(t²+1)+√2)], proving the exact threshold, equality case and strict example at t=13. Central symmetry gives both centroids zero; exposed base corners and apices give six vertices, while antipodal pairs must span dimension three. Independently triangulated the boundary and coned its triangles to the origin for tetrahedral volume quadrature; the three tested values agree, including surface 33.67898021143849 versus interior 33.8 at t=13 (replay /workspace/branches/independent_checks.js). This is finite corroboration only. The prior-work adjective non-tangential concerns the obstruction regime: K₁ itself has equal facet distances; this does not affect the theorem.

evidence: Pasteczka's positive cases include parallelotopes; Tokmachev requires a planar body with agreeing centroids or a circumscribed polytope with a common incenter and centroid. Lotnikov's three-dimensional basis is the anisotropically stretched convex hull of a square section and two octagonal caps.
broader_coverage.reasoning: In the reversal regime the bipyramid facet offsets t/√(t²+1) and t/√2 are unequal, so the centered-inball theorem does not apply. The earlier counterexample method applies to a different construction and does not give six vertices or the finite exact crossover.

evidence: For independent centered copies X,X', E|X−X'|²=2E|X|², and for Y,Y' likewise. Lotnikov's strict n=2 inequality gives E|X|²>E|Y|² and hence a direction u with E(u·X)²>E(u·Y)². Its spatial construction has octagonal end facets, each with eight vertices, not two apices.
claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: Qualitative central-symmetry failure for some quadratic, even for a polytope in the spatial construction, is covered by implication. The existence of a direction does not imply its occurrence on a vertex-minimal polytope or the threshold for the specified coordinates.

originality.rationale: Earlier work already gives the qualitative existence of centrally symmetric examples with a quadratic reversal: Lotnikov's n=2 inequality implies a second-moment trace reversal. The surviving distinction is the fixed coordinate quadratic, a sharp crossing in the explicit rectangular bipyramid, and attainment with the minimum six vertices. The strongest prior spatial construction uses a square and two octagonal caps; the closest same-day result is a positive theorem about products of balls. Neither supplies the six-vertex threshold.
residual_risks: Equivalent examples can be written in the language of anisotropically stretched octahedra or covariance differences; searches are not exhaustive. No priority for the qualitative reversal or classification of all six-vertex shapes is asserted.
